the identification of epigenetic changes that occur in the plasma of cancer patients, particularly in response to chemotherapy.

the study of plasma DNA methylation in ovarian cancer has been shown to be a useful tool for the study of the disease and its response to treatment.
hMLH1 DNA methylation is a marker of poor prognosis in patients with ovarian cancer.
hMLH1 hypermethylation in plasma DNA is associated with poor survival in patients with ovarian cancer.

the acquisition of hMLH methylation in plasma at relapse of ovarian cancer is an important predictor of survival, independent of time to relapse and age.
the acquisition of hMLH methylation in plasma at relapse predicts for poor overall survival in ovarian cancer patients, independent from age and time to progression.
the methylation of the MMR gene hMLH in the plasma DNA of patients treated with platinum/taxane chemotherapy predicts for poor survival.
